metadata.case_name: LAU HING KWAN v. LAI CHI KWAN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: office assistant-cum-messenger performing general office duties

injuries.description: geographic degloved injury to his forehead
source: he had sustained a geographic degloved injury to his forehead.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of head

injuries.description: minor head injury (post-concussional syndrome / features of PTSD)
source: In the accident on 21 July 2001, Mr Lau sustained a minor head injury.
Mr Lau has PCS as evidenced by the symptoms of headache, dizziness, impaired concentration, subjective impairment of cognition and memory and irritability.
He also has certain features of PTSD (see section 8.4) with severity well below that of the full-blown syndrome.

injuries.description: three areas of traumatic tattoos over his nose
source: It contained multiple telangiectusia. The scarring was also accompanied by three areas of traumatic tattoos over his nose.

manifestations.description: post traumatic amnesia of about eight hours
headache occurring about three or four times weekly, sometimes lasting for two hours, relieved by analgesics
subjective impairment of cognition and memory
moon-shaped scar over the forehead measuring 20 by 60 millimetres, containing multiple telangiectusia
cosmetic disfigurement of forehead and traumatic tattoos on nose
facial asymmetry (medial end of the right eyebrow displaced downwards) noted by Dr Gordon Ma
depression and loss of confidence; shies from social contact, becomes withdrawn

treatments_received: surgical debridement to the forehead wound
wound-cleansing (multiple sessions between 28 July and 10 September 2001)
insertion of a tissue expander under the forehead (5 August 2002)
weekly expansion of tissue expander (late August to end September 2002)
surgical removal of the expander and excision of the scar (30 September 2002)
surgical levelling of eyebrows (admitted 28 July 2003 and 4 August 2003)
photographs and follow-up at Prince of Wales Hospital
treatments_future: further laser treatment of the traumatic tattoos on the nose (indicated in report of 3 September 2004)

losses.description: He was very conscious of the moon-shaped scar and would frequently wear hats to conceal it; scarring over his forehead measured 20 by 60 millimetres and contained multiple telangiectusia; traumatic tattoos over his nose.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: He shies from social contact as a result of his disfigurement and would become particularly depressed when he hears of other traffic accidents; when out he would bow his head, wear a hat and avoid eye contact with other people.

Following the accident he has become somewhat withdrawn, preferring to remain at home to watch television or listen to music; once interested in jogging and swimming, he no longer pursues such interests.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Once interested in jogging and swimming activities, he said that he no longer pursues such interests.
He stated his memory has been impaired and he has impaired concentration and subjective impairment of cognition.

In the accident on 21 July 2001, Mr Lau sustained a minor head injury. Mr Lau has PCS as evidenced by the symptoms of headache, dizziness, impaired concentration, subjective impairment of cognition and memory and irritability. He also has certain features of PTSD (see section 8.4) with severity well below that of the full-blown syndrome.
